title: A work order with no parts shows Parts cost $0.00 and still closes
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location has no accounting integration (neither QuickBooks Online nor AccountingHub).
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Complete, with one approved labor line of 2.0 hours only, whose Shop supplies amount is $15.00.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The confirmation shows "Parts cost $0.00".
  • It shows "Shop supplies $15.00".

Step 3:

  • The work order shows the status Closed with its document.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11767 (Story 10, Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders)

  • S3-E1: “If the work order has no parts, the confirmation shows "Parts cost $0.00"; Close posts no parts entry, posts the shop supplies entry when the amount is above $0.00 (S10-E2), and still creates the internal invoice.”
  • S10-E2: “A work order with no parts and no labor still posts its shop supplies amount if it is above $0.00.”
